excerpts.author: kevaundray
excerpts.content:
Not sure if you figured it out, here’s how I think of it.

If you have a bound on b, you can ignore the modulo part and add the appropriate multiple of q to -b. So you would have [a + (mq-b)] * c mod q

This is the same since expanded you have (ac + cmq - bc) mod q = (ac + 0 - bc ) mod q = (a-b)*c mod q

What you did was reduce b mod q first, so that b < q. Making the value for m always be 1.
